title: Model switches in the chat — a divider instead of a bubble

steps.path: A Claude Code chat, after switching model from the model picker
steps.headline: Switching model now shows a thin "Model switched to Opus" line, not a "/model opus[1m]" message from you.
steps.changed: The switch used to appear as a chat bubble, as if you had typed a command to Claude. It is now the same thin divider the chat already uses for "Conversation cleared", with the time it happened.
steps.notice: It appears however you switch: the model picker, Shift+Space or typing /model. It stays when you reopen the chat, and on your phone. Pressing Shift+Space three times in a row leaves one line naming where you landed.
steps.risk: If a Claude Code update rewords its "Set model to" reply, the line stops appearing until the app is updated (the status bar label still changes).

steps.path: A chat with any other provider (OpenRouter, ChatGPT, a local model), after picking a different model
steps.headline: Chats with other providers now record each model switch too, with the same line.
steps.changed: These chats used to leave no trace of a switch: only the status bar label changed. They now save a "Model switched to …" line in the conversation itself, named the way the status bar names the model.
steps.notice: You can scroll back and see which model wrote which replies, in both kinds of chat, and the history survives closing and reopening.
steps.risk: Switches made before this update were never saved, so older chats show no line for them.
